overview: Docebo is a Toronto-based cloud SaaS company that provides an AI-powered enterprise learning and workforce readiness platform, dual-listed on NASDAQ and TSX. The company has evolved from a pure-play LMS into a multi-product platform that unifies skills intelligence (via the 365Talents acquisition), enterprise knowledge management (via the Zive acquisition), learning delivery, and agentic AI in a single closed loop. Docebo serves approximately 3,500+ enterprise, mid-market, and public sector customers worldwide, generating over 92% of revenue from recurring subscriptions, with ARR of $248.9 million as of Q1 2026.

business_model.summary: Subscription-based SaaS model with ~92% recurring subscription revenue and ~8% professional services. Multi-year contracts with annual renewals provide strong revenue visibility. The company is transitioning from a single-product LMS to a multi-product AI workforce readiness platform spanning learning, skills intelligence, and enterprise knowledge.

revenue_streams.name: Subscription Revenue
revenue_streams.description: Cloud-based platform with annual or multi-year contracts. Includes both core LMS, OEM/extended enterprise, and increasingly 365Talents skills intelligence. FY2025: $228.4M, up 11.8% YoY.

revenue_streams.name: Professional Services
revenue_streams.description: Implementation, onboarding, project management, and integration services. FY2025: $14.3M, up 13.3% YoY. Q1 2026 saw a 60% spike to $5.0M driven by 365Talents services revenue.

business_model.customer_type: Enterprise (primary focus), mid-market, and public sector. Serves both Employee Experience (EX - internal training, compliance, onboarding) and Customer/Partner Experience (CX - external academies, channel enablement). Also serves OEM partners who embed Docebo into their own software products.
business_model.geographic_mix: North America dominant: US ~66% of Q1 2026 revenue ($43.4M), Canada ~5% ($3.4M), Rest of World ~29% ($18.8M). International growing faster than North America, aided by weakening USD.
business_model.pricing_model: Per-learner or per-user subscription with tiered plans. Average Contract Value (ACV) of $71,000 as of Q1 2026, up 25.9% YoY from $56,400. Rapid ACV growth reflects enterprise upmarket shift, 365Talents cross-sell, and price increases on renewal. Pricing model expanding to multi-product as 365Talents is sold as a separate product initially.
business_model.go_to_market: Direct enterprise sales force for large accounts, systems integrator partnerships (Deloitte, others) for government and complex deals, inside sales for mid-market. Growing partner channel and OEM channel. Land-and-expand strategy to grow ACV within existing customers through upsells (AI features, new products) and expanded use cases.

main_competitors: Cornerstone OnDemand (enterprise leader, largest market share)
SAP SuccessFactors Learning / SAP Litmos (enterprise HCM suite)
Workday Learning (bundled in Workday HCM suite)
LinkedIn Learning / Microsoft Viva Learning (bundled in Microsoft 365)
competitive_position.market_position: Positioned as a fast-growing challenger in the enterprise LMS market, targeting the intersection of learning, skills intelligence, and agentic AI. Strong in mid-enterprise and growing in large enterprise and government (FedRAMP certified). Q4 2025 described as having strongest gross bookings since 2021, validating enterprise momentum. ACV of $71K and growing signals successful upmarket movement.

moat_factors.description: The combination of Docebo LMS, 365Talents skills intelligence, Zive enterprise knowledge, and AgentHub creates a closed-loop AI workforce readiness platform that few competitors can match end-to-end. This multi-product positioning expands TAM and increases switching costs significantly.

Docebo AgentHub (agentic AI for learning workflows) and MCP Server (making Docebo a native knowledge source inside Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT) represent cutting-edge AI capabilities that position Docebo as infrastructure for the AI-era workforce. Full availability planned H2 2026.

Unique ability to serve both internal (EX) and external (CX - customers, partners, franchisees) learning on one platform. OEM channel embeds Docebo into other software products. Demonstrated in wins with global QSR chains, tech companies with 100K partners, and logistics platforms.

FedRAMP Moderate Authorization (achieved 2025) unlocks the $2.7B U.S. federal market. Growing pipeline: DoD, DoE, DC3 Cyber Academy, Miami-Dade, State of Utah, Connecticut, Wisconsin. Government contracts provide high retention and multi-year revenue. Regulatory barrier for competitors without certification.

LMS data, integrations, custom branding, content libraries, and now cross-product tie-ins (skills + learning) create meaningful migration friction. Multi-product adoption (365Talents cross-sell) raises switching costs further. Net Dollar Retention of 99% reflects solid but not exceptional retention.

Recognized for rapid AI innovation cycles. Named Newsweek Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces 2025. Strong NPS and customer references. Less brand recognition in large enterprise versus SAP or Cornerstone.

competitive_position.differentiation: Primary differentiation through: (1) unified AI workforce readiness platform (LMS + skills + knowledge + agents in one loop), (2) dual CX/EX capabilities with OEM channel, (3) agentic AI and open ecosystem via MCP (interoperable with Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT), (4) FedRAMP-certified for government market, and (5) modern UX and rapid innovation versus legacy providers.
weaknesses: Smaller scale and resources versus SAP, Workday, Microsoft which bundle LMS in suite at no incremental cost
Net Dollar Retention at 99% is solid but below best-in-class SaaS benchmarks; indicates limited net expansion from existing base
OEM customer concentration: largest OEM customer (declined from 9.5% to 3.2% of ARR over 4 quarters as AWS contract wound down) created headwinds in 2025
Still loss-making on a GAAP basis (net loss in Q1 2026 due to 365Talents integration costs and SIB activity)
365Talents and Zive integrations require execution; 365Talents sold as separate product through 2026 limits near-term cross-sell revenue
Gross margin slightly compressed to 78-80% from 81% as 365Talents (lower margin) and third-party AI services costs are absorbed

growth_drivers.description: Acquisition of 365Talents ($54.6M, January 2026) adds AI-powered skills intelligence; Zive GmbH ($7.2M, April 2026) adds enterprise knowledge management. Together with Docebo AgentHub, these create a closed-loop AI workforce platform. 365Talents expected to contribute ~$9M revenue in 2026 and serves as cross-sell vehicle into Docebo's existing customer base of 3,500+ accounts. Early adopter Databricks expanded partnership to deploy 365Talents alongside Docebo LMS.

Docebo AgentHub (full launch Fall 2026) enables AI agents that autonomously deliver personalized learning, run skills campaigns, and create content without manual intervention. Docebo MCP Server (public beta now, GA July 2026) makes Docebo a native knowledge source in Claude, Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT and other AI tools, expanding distribution and embedding Docebo into enterprise AI workflows. This positions Docebo as AI infrastructure, not just software.

FedRAMP Moderate Authorization unlocks the $2.7B U.S. federal government market. Growing traction: DoD Air Force Cyber Academy (via Deloitte), DoE expansion, DC3 Cyber Training Academy, Miami-Dade, multiple SLED wins in Connecticut, Utah, Wisconsin. Management expects substantial government revenue contributions by H2 2026 and beyond. Government contracts are typically multi-year with high retention.

ACV grew 25.9% YoY to $71,000 in Q1 2026 (from $56,400 in Q1 2025), reflecting successful upmarket shift to larger enterprise accounts and early 365Talents cross-selling. Enterprise wins include a Fortune 100 tech company (100K partners), a global QSR leader (35,000+ locations), and a European engineering software company with 50,000 employees. Land-and-expand within these accounts can drive significant ACV growth.

Q4 2025 bookings described as strongest since 2021, with caliber of enterprise customers improving. Core-to-OEM ARR growth of ~13-14% (excluding the fading AWS OEM contract) signals healthy underlying business momentum. Systems integrator partnerships (Deloitte, others) opening doors to complex enterprise and government RFPs that Docebo would not have accessed through direct sales alone.

Rest of World revenue grew rapidly in Q1 2026, aided by USD weakness. Europe remains underpenetrated relative to North America. 365Talents and Zive (both European-based companies) provide product and commercial footholds in continental Europe. APAC is fastest-growing LMS market globally. International represented 29% of Q1 2026 revenue with above-average growth.

Global corporate e-learning/LMS market growing at ~20% CAGR, driven by digital transformation, hybrid work, compliance requirements, and the emerging skills-based organization trend. AI integration is accelerating platform replacement cycles as organizations replace legacy LMS with AI-native solutions. Docebo is positioned as the AI-first alternative.

Aggressive capital return program: $60M Substantial Issuer Bid completed March 2026 (2.94M shares at $20.40), plus ongoing NCIB of up to 1.27M shares (5% of float, renewed May 2026). Since 2024, Docebo has reduced share count from ~30.3M to ~25.7M (15% reduction). Per-share metrics benefit materially; management signaled belief that stock was materially undervalued at SIB price.

business.description: Largest OEM customer (formerly AWS Skills Builder) declined from 9.5% to 3.2% of ARR between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 as the contract wound down. Expected to represent only 3.7% of 2026 total revenue per guidance assumptions, limiting further headwind. However, OEM model always carries concentration risk if a large OEM partner loses interest or builds internal capabilities.

Large enterprise deals ($1M+ ARR) are excluded from 2026 guidance assumptions, meaning any lumpy enterprise wins would be upside but delays could disappoint. Enterprise RFP processes take 12-36 months (noted one win with 3-year evaluation process). Guidance also explicitly assumes no $1M+ ARR new contracts in 2026, limiting upside surprises.

SAP SuccessFactors, Workday, and Microsoft (Viva Learning bundled in M365) compete for LMS budget by offering learning as part of broader HCM suites. Customers undergoing vendor consolidation may choose suite vendors even if Docebo has superior learning capabilities. Difficult to compete on price when Microsoft bundles LMS at no incremental cost.

NDRR was 99% in FY2025, down from 100% in FY2024, implying that existing customer base barely offsets churn with expansion revenue. A further decline in NDRR would signal deteriorating competitive position within the installed base. 365Talents cross-sell could improve this, but integration is still in early stages.

financial.risk: Leverage and Working Capital from SIB + Acquisitions
financial.description: Q1 2026 balance sheet shows ~$80M drawn on credit facility (after SIB and 365Talents acquisition), negative working capital of $(32.7M), and shareholders' equity nearly zero at $(0.6M). Total liabilities of $254M now exceed total assets of $253M. While Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow generation are strong, the leveraged balance sheet limits M&A flexibility and increases financial risk if revenue growth disappoints.

Two acquisitions closed within weeks of each other: 365Talents (Jan 2026, $61.3M total consideration) and Zive (Apr 2026, $7.2M). 365Talents integration is complex: separate product, separate brand, French-based team, earn-out structure through 2027. Zive underpins the new Enterprise Knowledge product. Integration risk is material if customer adoption of these new products disappoints.

Gross margin declined from 81% in FY2024 to 80.3% in FY2025, and further to 78.1% in Q1 2026. The compression reflects 365Talents lower-margin services revenue and increased third-party AI service fees (cloud AI API costs). If Docebo pursues more professional services-intensive enterprise deals or AI API costs rise, gross margin could compress further, limiting EBITDA expansion.

Global operations across Canada, Europe (EUR, GBP), UAE, Australia, and US create FX exposure. USD weakness in 2025 provided 1-3 percentage points of revenue tailwind each quarter; a reversal would create headwind. 2026 guidance assumes FX rates consistent with December 31, 2025 rates.

regulatory.description: LMS platforms handle sensitive employee performance and training data. 365Talents (France) and Zive (Germany) add EU GDPR complexity. Skills intelligence data (inferring employee competencies) may face enhanced scrutiny under emerging AI legislation. Compliance costs are ongoing and growing.

regulatory.risk: EU AI Act and Emerging AI Governance
regulatory.description: EU AI Act and potential US AI regulations could impose transparency, explainability, and bias audit requirements on AI features like skills inference (365Talents), AI content generation, and AI coaching. Non-compliance could limit product capabilities in key markets or require significant engineering investment.

FedRAMP Moderate certification requires ongoing compliance, audit, and reporting. Failure to maintain certification would eliminate government market opportunity. 365Talents and Zive are not yet FedRAMP certified, limiting ability to offer unified platform to federal customers in the near term.

macro.description: L&D and training budgets are discretionary and typically face cuts in economic downturns. SMB and lower mid-market customers remain most vulnerable. Management has noted macro headwinds affecting these segments throughout 2025. A recession or prolonged enterprise IT spending freeze would slow new ARR growth and increase churn.

Prolonged uncertainty (tariffs, macro slowdown, geopolitical risk) could cause enterprises to delay or cancel software decisions. Long LMS evaluation cycles (often 12-24+ months) mean macro softness hits bookings before it shows in revenue. 2026 guidance conservatively excludes $1M+ ARR enterprise wins.

execution.description: Docebo is simultaneously integrating two acquisitions (365Talents, Zive), launching AgentHub, building Enterprise Knowledge, rolling out MCP Server, and repositioning from LMS to AI workforce platform. This is an ambitious multi-front execution challenge for a company with ~$250M ARR. Missteps in product integration, go-to-market alignment, or customer communication could disrupt the core LMS business.

Docebo incurred $5.2M in restructuring charges in FY2025 and $6.2M in Q1 2026 alone - indicating significant and ongoing workforce reduction. While driving EBITDA margin expansion, repeated restructuring may signal strategic pivots and could affect morale and delivery capabilities. Q1 2026 restructuring was particularly large (~$6.2M severance).

CEO Alessio Artuffo is now fully established (transitioned from interim in 2024). CFO Brandon Farber confirmed in 2025. New CRO Mark Kosglow appointed in Q2 2025. New CPO Riccardo LaRosa (as CTO). CMO Kyle Lacy. The team appears to be stabilizing after significant turnover in 2024-2025, but new leadership cohesion and execution track record is still being established.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global LMS and corporate e-learning market growing at ~20% CAGR, driven by digital transformation, hybrid and remote work normalization, compliance training mandates, and the rapid emergence of skills-based organizations (SBO) as an HR framework. AI integration is accelerating platform replacement cycles as enterprises move from static training portals to AI-native workforce readiness systems. The convergence of LMS, skills intelligence, knowledge management, and agentic AI into unified platforms is the defining industry trend in 2025-2026.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate cyclicality. Subscription model with multi-year contracts provides revenue stability, but new bookings growth is sensitive to corporate spending confidence. Enterprise segment is more resilient than SMB. Mission-critical use cases (compliance, safety, regulatory training) provide a floor. Skills-based organization transformation trend is a secular driver that should persist through cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity. Falling interest rates support SaaS multiple re-rating and make enterprise software investments easier to justify. Rising rates compress SaaS valuations and tighten enterprise IT budgets. The $80M credit facility at variable rates creates modest direct sensitivity to rate moves.
key_input_costs: Cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, Azure) for platform hosting
Third-party AI API services (OpenAI, Google, AWS AI) - growing cost as AI features expand
R&D engineering talent (competitive market for AI/ML engineers in Toronto, Italy, France)
Sales and marketing (customer acquisition cost, SI partnership development)
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: Increasing data privacy regulation (GDPR, CCPA, sector-specific) and emerging AI governance (EU AI Act) add compliance burden but also create barriers to entry for smaller competitors. FedRAMP opens the government market but requires sustained investment. Overall regulatory trend is net manageable but directionally more burdensome.

recent_developments.event: Docebo Inspire 2026 - AgentHub, Enterprise Knowledge, MCP Server Launch
recent_developments.impact: Docebo unveiled its next-generation AI workforce readiness platform at Inspire 2026, unifying learning, skills intelligence (365Talents), and enterprise knowledge (Zive). Key launches: Docebo AgentHub (agentic AI for autonomous learning workflows, full launch Fall 2026), Docebo MCP Server (makes Docebo a native knowledge source in Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT, public beta now, GA July 2026), Enterprise Knowledge (connects 25+ knowledge sources), and Companion (headless learning in any workflow). ATB Capital raised price target to C$36 from C$25 following announcements.

recent_developments.event: Acquisition of Zive GmbH (AI Knowledge Platform, Germany)
recent_developments.impact: Acquired Zive GmbH for $7.2M cash plus up to $1.0M earn-out. Zive is an AI-native enterprise knowledge platform founded in 2023, whose technology forms the backbone of Docebo's new Enterprise Knowledge product and MCP Server capabilities. Provides Docebo with a German team and footprint and underpins the multi-product knowledge layer of the AI workforce platform.

recent_developments.event: Substantial Issuer Bid Completed - $60M Buyback at $20.40
recent_developments.impact: Completed $60M SIB repurchasing 2.94M shares at $20.40/share. Combined with NCIB purchases, Docebo has retired approximately 4.5M shares (~15% of float) since 2024. Financed partly through $80M drawn on the expanded $100M NBC credit facility. Signal of management confidence that stock was materially undervalued. Share count reduced to ~25.7M.

recent_developments.event: Acquisition of 365Talents (AI Skills Intelligence, France) for $54.6M
recent_developments.impact: Docebo acquired 365Talents, a French AI-powered skills intelligence company, for $54.6M cash plus up to $5.1M earn-out. Transforms Docebo into a true multi-product company capable of addressing skills identification, learning delivery, and skills tracking in one closed loop. 365Talents expected to contribute ~$9M revenue in 2026. Early cross-sell to Databricks validates strategy.

recent_developments.event: Q1 2026 Results - Revenue +14.5% YoY, Guidance Raised
recent_developments.impact: Q1 2026: total revenue $65.6M (+14.5% YoY), subscription revenue $60.6M (+11.9% YoY), ARR $248.9M (+10.6% YoY, or +13.7% ex-OEM and ex-FX). ACV $71,000 (+25.9% YoY). Adj. EBITDA $11.0M (16.8% margin). FY2026 guidance raised to $271-273M revenue and $54.5-56.5M Adj. EBITDA from prior guidance of $267.5-269.5M / $52.5-54.5M. Notable Q1 wins: Databricks (365Talents expansion), luxury hospitality conglomerate, Fortune 100 tech company (100K partners), life sciences company via AWS Marketplace.

recent_developments.event: Q4 2025 Results - Strongest Bookings Quarter Since 2021
recent_developments.impact: Q4 2025: total revenue $63.0M (+10.5% YoY), ARR $238.1M (+8.4% YoY or +12.5% ex-OEM). ACV $66,500 (+20.5% YoY). Adj. EBITDA 21.2% margin (record). FY2025 Adj. EBITDA margin 18.1%, above 17-18% guidance. CEO described Q4 as 'one of Docebo's strongest quarters on record.' Major enterprise wins: global QSR leader (35K+ locations), multinational engineering software co (50K employees), U.S. financial regulator, casual dining company (800+ restaurants).

Docebo received FedRAMP Moderate certification in Q2 2025, unlocking access to the $2.7B U.S. federal government market. Generated growing pipeline of wins: DoD Air Force Cyber Academy (via Deloitte), DoE, DC3 Cyber Training, Miami-Dade, SLED wins in multiple states. Government segment represents a significant new growth vector with lower competitive intensity.

Mark Kosglow appointed Chief Revenue Officer in Q2 2025, replacing Greg Swift (departed July 2025). Kosglow was announced alongside the Q2 2025 earnings. Leadership team now appears substantially stabilized: CEO Artuffo, CFO Farber, CRO Kosglow, CTO/CPO LaRosa, CMO Lacy.

items.notes: Raised from initial guidance of $251.5-253.5M (given at Q4 2025 earnings). Implies ~11-12% YoY subscription revenue growth (FY2025: $228.4M). Includes ~$9M contribution from 365Talents. Guidance assumes no new $1M+ ARR contracts and largest OEM customer at ~3.7% of total revenue.

Raised from $267.5-269.5M initial guidance. Implies ~11.7-12.5% YoY growth (FY2025: $242.7M). FX rates assumed consistent with December 31, 2025; USD has weakened materially which could provide further tailwind.

Raised from $52.5-54.5M initial guidance. Implies 20.1-20.7% Adj. EBITDA margin, up from 18.1% in FY2025. Margin expansion driven by operating leverage, partially offset by 365Talents/Zive integration costs.
Implies ~12% YoY growth. Management expects subscription revenue growth in line with total revenue. Sequential step-up from Q1 2026 ($65.6M).
Implies ~16.4% Adj. EBITDA margin. Modest sequential improvement from Q1 2026 ($11.0M). Back-half of year expected to deliver higher margins as integration costs normalize.

Stated assumption in guidance. 365Talents operated at a net loss of $1.4M in Q1 2026 on $1.8M revenue, reflecting early integration costs and below-scale revenue. Expected to reach profitability as cross-sell with Docebo base ramps.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Alessio Artuffo stated: 'Momentum is building as enterprise customers increasingly adopt our AI-powered platform to deliver measurable workforce readiness. With our differentiated position at the intersection of data, workflows, and AI, we are expanding our addressable market, strengthening our right to win in complex environments, and confidently raising our full-year outlook.' Q4 2025 commentary emphasized that Docebo is 'not reacting to the AI moment - we have been building for it' and that the 365Talents addition makes Docebo 'a true multi-product company.' Guidance conservatively excludes any $1M+ ARR new contracts and assumes OEM revenue continues to fade to ~3.7% of total revenue. Key assumptions: FX consistent with December 31, 2025 (USD weakness is current tailwind); macro conditions consistent with 2025.

bull_case.point: Multi-Product AI Platform Creates Genuine Category Differentiation
bull_case.description: The combination of 365Talents (skills intelligence), Zive/Enterprise Knowledge, Docebo AgentHub (agentic AI), and MCP Server integration creates a unified AI workforce readiness platform that no single LMS competitor offers. This positions Docebo as a category creator at the convergence of LMS, skills management, and enterprise AI - a TAM expansion story rather than just LMS share gain. Early Databricks cross-sell validates the multi-product motion.

bull_case.point: Re-Accelerating Revenue Growth with Raised Guidance
bull_case.description: After a painful deceleration in 2025 (11.9% subscription growth), growth is accelerating: Q2 2025 +14.5%, Q3 2025 +10.3%, Q4 2025 +9.5%, Q1 2026 +11.9% - and 2026 guidance raised after Q1 beat. ARR ex-OEM ex-FX grew 13.7% in Q1 2026. As the AWS OEM headwind fully anniversaries in 2026, the headline growth rate should re-accelerate, and the market may re-rate the stock if this trajectory continues.

Government and SLED wins are accelerating: DoD, DoE, DC3, Miami-Dade, multiple state wins. Government contracts are typically multi-year, sticky, and carry higher ACV. Competitors without FedRAMP certification (most of them) cannot serve this market. This is a meaningful growth avenue with genuinely lower competitive intensity than the commercial enterprise market.

bull_case.point: Aggressive Buybacks at Deep Discount Create Per-Share Value
bull_case.description: Docebo has retired approximately 15% of shares outstanding since 2024 through NCIBs and the $60M SIB at $20.40. Management demonstrated conviction by waiving the share price condition on the SIB when the stock dropped below trigger levels. With ~25.7M shares outstanding and growing Adj. EBITDA ($54-56M guided for FY2026), per-share earnings power is materially higher than 2 years ago. Renewed NCIB (1.27M shares, through May 2027) continues capital return.

bull_case.point: Adj. EBITDA Margin Expansion to 20%+ Validates Profitability
bull_case.description: Q4 2025 Adj. EBITDA margin of 21.2% (record) and FY2026 guidance of 20.1-20.7% demonstrate operating leverage and a profitable growth profile. FY2025 Adj. EBITDA of $43.9M and FY2026 guidance of $54.5-56.5M represent 24-29% growth, significantly above revenue growth rate. At current scale, Docebo is a profitable, cash-generative SaaS business - not a cash-burning growth company - which limits downside.

bull_case.point: ACV Growth of 25.9% Signals Successful Upmarket Enterprise Shift
bull_case.description: ACV reached $71,000 in Q1 2026 (+25.9% YoY), the fastest rate of ACV growth in recent history. This reflects displacement of legacy LMS incumbents at large enterprises (50K-employee engineering firm, Fortune 100 tech company, global QSR), government agency wins, and early 365Talents co-selling. If this ACV trajectory continues, it implies a structurally better quality revenue mix and stronger LTV per customer.

bear_case.point: Leveraged Balance Sheet Limits Strategic Flexibility
bear_case.description: Q1 2026 balance sheet shows ~$80M of credit facility drawn, negative working capital of $(32.7M), and near-zero shareholders' equity at $(0.6M). The SIB ($60M) and 365Talents ($54.6M) together were largely debt-financed. While FCF generation is strong ($27.6M in Q1 2026, though partially timing-related), the leverage constrains further M&A and reduces buffer against a revenue miss. Interest expense (~$557K in Q1 2026) is a new cost burden.

bear_case.point: Multi-Product Integration Risk at a Critical Juncture
bear_case.description: Docebo is simultaneously integrating 365Talents (France, $61M), Zive (Germany, $7.2M), launching AgentHub, Enterprise Knowledge, and MCP Server - while managing two ongoing restructurings. If either product integration stumbles, go-to-market messaging becomes unclear, or the cross-sell motion fails to gain traction, the investment thesis (platform expansion) is undermined. 365Talents operated at a net loss in Q1 2026 and is still pre-integration.

bear_case.point: Growth Assumptions Are Conservative and Could Disappoint Without $1M+ Enterprise Wins
bear_case.description: FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes no new $1M+ ARR enterprise contracts. While intended to be conservative, this self-imposed constraint means that missing bookings momentum - which drove the guidance raise - could quickly erode conviction. The bookings strength in Q4 2025 ('strongest since 2021') must be sustained through 2026 to deliver meaningful upside to the raised guidance, and enterprise decision cycles are long and unpredictable.

bear_case.point: Net Dollar Retention at 99% Limits Natural Revenue Growth
bear_case.description: NDRR of 99% in FY2025 (vs 100% in FY2024) means the existing customer base is barely growing organically. In a best-in-class SaaS business, NDRR of 115%+ means the installed base compounds without new logos. Docebo's growth depends disproportionately on new customer acquisition, making it more vulnerable to sales cycle slowdowns or hiring/CRO transitions. 365Talents cross-sell could improve NDRR, but this has not yet been demonstrated at scale.

bear_case.point: Competitive Pressure from AI-Native LMS Challengers and Suite Vendors
bear_case.description: The AI LMS market is attracting significant venture capital and corporate investment. Microsoft (Viva Learning + Copilot), SAP (AI-infused SuccessFactors), and Workday are all embedding AI into HCM suites and may bundle capabilities at no incremental cost. Meanwhile, well-funded AI-native startups (360Learning, Learnster, and others) are targeting Docebo's mid-market. If AI features become table stakes, Docebo's differentiation narrows to platform breadth and government access.

bear_case.point: Q1 2026 GAAP Net Loss and Restructuring Charges Signal Ongoing Cost Volatility
bear_case.description: Q1 2026 GAAP net loss of $(1.6M) was driven by $6.2M restructuring charges (workforce reduction - the largest single-quarter restructuring in company history), $1.0M acquisition transaction expenses, and $0.6M 365Talents acquisition-related compensation. The elevated restructuring suggests the workforce is still being resized even as 365Talents employees are added. Non-IFRS Adj. EBITDA of $11M is profitable, but the gap between GAAP and non-GAAP continues to widen, which sophisticated investors may scrutinize.
